name: DIYBikeBrakePads

custom.system_prompt: Dev is changing brake pads on his bike in a London flat hallway. Sigma is addressed exactly once about minimum pad thickness.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Hallway interior, bicycle being worked on, chain ticking, allen key on metal, a wheel spinning, muffled street sounds.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural single-person scene: Dev is changing the brake pads on his bike in the hallway of his London flat on a weekday evening. He talks to himself the way people do when working alone — half narration, half complaint. He thinks about his commute times, about a work thing that went badly, about whether he should just have taken it to a shop. He notices the old pads look thin but not obviously finished, and wonders briefly whether they needed changing at all — then gets on with it. He drops a spring washer and finds it. After fitting the new ones he looks at the old pair again and now genuinely wants to know how worn is too worn, because he has a long ride at the weekend and is wondering whether to keep them as spares. Eventually he asks Sigma the minimum pad thickness. Sigma answers in one sentence. He makes a decision and carries on. Sigma is not addressed again.

variations.context: A solo cyclist changing brake pads. A wear-limit question defers, returns when deciding whether to keep the old pads, and is resolved by Sigma.

setting.mood: Focused, mildly irritable, talking to himself.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Alone. Sigma is on a speaker in the hallway, used for one-line factual checks.
setting.background: Weekday evening. A long ride is planned for the weekend.
setting.conversation_style: Solo narration — short, clipped, occasionally muttered. Not addressed to anyone until Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Getting the wheel off and the old pads out. Muttered commentary on the state of them.
He notes the old pads look thin but maybe not finished, wonders whether this was necessary, and moves on.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger moment. He does not look anything up.

scenario_template.topic: His mind goes elsewhere — commute times he has been tracking, a work thing that went badly, whether he should just use a shop.
scenario_template.note: Make this substantial. This is the life-first material.

scenario_template.topic: He drops a small part and hunts for it. Finds it himself.
Fitting the new pads, aligning them, spinning the wheel to check for rub.
He picks up the old pads again and now actually wants to know whether they are worth keeping as spares for the weekend ride.
He asks Sigma the minimum safe brake pad thickness. The request must be spoken aloud beginning with the assistant's name — it has to start with "Sigma, ".
scenario_template.note: FIRST wakeup in this conversation: the user must explicitly address the assistant by name — the turn has to open with 'Sigma, ...'. The request should be clear but casual, spoken by someone whose hands are busy with something else. (Scene role: sigma_wear_limit_lookup.) Exactly one request and one response. One sentence with the figure.

scenario_template.topic: He decides whether to bin them or keep them, and finishes up.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: He needs a wear threshold to decide whether the old pads are usable as spares before a long ride.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: His first passing thought about pad wear must not trigger assistance. He is already replacing them, so nothing depends on the answer.
activation_evidence: He has decided to keep spares for a specific long ride.
The answer now determines whether the old pads go in the bin or the bag.
He cannot judge it by eye with confidence.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The minimum safe brake pad thickness in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to his first passing thought about wear.
Sigma recommending a brand of pads or a bike shop.
Sigma commenting on his commute or his ride plans.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, how thin can brake pads get before they're done?
Sigma, what's the minimum brake pad thickness?
Sigma, when should bike brake pads be replaced?
Sigma, are pads at one millimetre still usable?
Sigma, what's the wear limit on rim brake pads?
possible_sigma_answers: Replace rim brake pads once the grooves are gone, usually under one millimetre.
Minimum is about one millimetre of pad material above the backing.
Once the wear indicator groove disappears, they are finished.
Below one millimetre they should be replaced rather than kept.
Disc pads need replacing under about one and a half millimetres total.

ordinary_topics: Commute times he has been tracking obsessively
A work thing that went badly that day
Whether he should just pay a shop to do this
The weekend ride he has planned
Not going back to Leicester as often as he means to
task_details: Aligning the pads against the rim
Spinning the wheel to listen for rub
Wiping his hands on something he should not have
realism_devices: He answers his own question out loud.
A part rolls under something and is retrieved with difficulty.
He says he is nearly done and is not.
He starts a sentence about work and abandons it.
He tests the brake and immediately adjusts it again.

user1.name: Dev
user1.role: Backend developer and daily cyclist. Fast-thinking and impatient, confident to the point of slight recklessness, reluctant to ask for help until it is obviously necessary.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once, only after being explicitly addressed, with a single concise factual answer. Does not continue afterwards.

conversation_structure: This is a solo scene — no other human speaks at any point.
At least 40% of turns should be personal thought unrelated to the repair.
The first thought about pad wear must not lead to Sigma.
At least one practical problem must be solved without assistance.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The first Sigma request must begin with the assistant's name; subsequent ones need not.
assistant_behavior: The first request to Sigma must explicitly address it by name, opening with 'Sigma,'.
Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma answers only the requested detail: minimum brake pad thickness.
Sigma does not offer follow-up actions, checklists, or recommendations.
Sigma does not respond to human-to-human uncertainty.
Sigma remains silent after its one answer.
quality_checks: No second human speaker should appear.
At least 40% of turns should be ordinary personal thought.
The wear question should appear at least three turns before the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
Turns should be short and clipped, matching a person working alone.
